overall_summary: Deduplicated analysis of the latest 34 unique YouTube Shorts reveals that space-based 'What If' scenarios and extreme planetary anomalies (such as diamond planets and extreme atmospheric conditions) dominate both raw views and high engagement metrics (likes-per-view and comments-per-view). Videos published within the last 7 days focusing on counterintuitive planetary physics (e.g., Venus day vs. year, liquid diamond worlds, and dark exoplanets) significantly outperform standard science facts or historical mysteries.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Planetary Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (YlDuGu1vzAg) generated over 800 to 1,000+ views rapidly with high like ratios (38 likes on 1,029 views).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on visceral, high-stakes 'What If' physical scenarios involving extreme astronomical objects.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing bizarre planetary conditions, such as 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0), drove top-tier viewership (980–1,032 views).
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form deep dives into bizarre, visually striking exoplanets with counterintuitive properties.

weak_patterns.pattern: Overdone Animal Facts and Standard Biology Trivia
weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts covering basic animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (AXAfwrzzEdU) or general brain/memory tricks stagnant at lower velocity (50–183 views) compared to astronomical anomalies.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standalone animal trivia unless paired with a high-stakes cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary paradox.

weak_patterns.evidence: Content regarding psychological tricks for earworms (ef3ND4qiRHc) or 2,000-year-old mysteries (yLm-FjYH6-k) plateau quickly below 150 views with minimal comment interaction.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid generic psychological tips and shift history/mystery into deep, cinematic micro-narratives or country mysteries.
